headline: High-risk shared-state and output-trust issues: Plandex can write shared project state while Rasa can relay unverified content to external channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads/writes a project directory and uses a review-then-apply flow with shared state via the Plandex server backend; Rasa can surface text/voice content through messaging channels. If Rasa content is copied into Plandex inputs or shared files, instruction-like payloads can influence planning. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Rasa messages are copied into Plandex prompts or files
IF both agents read the same project directory or shared backend state
mitigations: Disable any shared workspace between the agents
Require manual sanitization before copying Rasa content into Plandex
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code and model-provider API keys and can read/write the project directory; Rasa handles text and voice and can send data through allowlisted network egress to messaging APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive code or conversation data can flow between them. No direct shared-storage mechanism is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem workspace
IF Rasa forwards conversation content that includes secrets or code snippets
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials immediately
Restrict Rasa channels to non-sensitive test traffic
Remove secrets from any shared project directory
Use per-agent network egress allowlists
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before cross-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Rasa is a multi-instance chatbot framework with allowlisted egress. If both operate on the same mutable repo or deployment artifacts, concurrent writes can clobber state or create inconsistent releases. The conflict is plausible from the profiles, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or deployment directory
IF Rasa instances and Plandex sessions run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes git state
Use file locks or a single-writer queue
Review and merge changes manually before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex produces staged changes and plans; Rasa is a dialogue system that can emit responses to users or downstream channels. If Rasa treats Plandex output as authoritative, a mistaken plan or code suggestion can cascade into incorrect user-facing actions or messages. The interaction is inferred, but the default review-then-apply flow does not eliminate the risk.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes Plandex output without verification
IF Plandex-generated text is forwarded into customer-facing replies or automations
mitigations: Require human review before Rasa uses Plandex output
Add schema validation for any handoff payload
Limit Plandex output to non-authoritative drafts
Log and diff all cross-agent transfers
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys, while Rasa handles text and voice and can transmit through messaging platforms. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: cross-channel logging or retention could diverge if the same data class is shared. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair's combined handling.
conditions: IF the same customer or secret-bearing data is routed through both agents
IF one agent logs or retains messages longer than the other
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through both agents
Set short retention on shared logs
Review channel-specific privacy settings
Separate secret-bearing code workflows from support workflows
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
